frontier.hypothesis: A second SET of `idx` placed OUTSIDE the loops denies the birthing_insn_p lift at zero instruction cost, and porting it onto the JD chassis closes JD outright.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c's birthing_insn_p gives a priority bonus to a set of a pseudo with reg_n_sets == 1; a second set anywhere in the function removes it. Session 8's sweep25 KD measured exactly this (a second set outside the loops) at 4/78 with the loop top EXACT -- but on the older chassis, where the remaining points were the sum/halfword ones JD does not have. JD's residual IS the loop top and nothing else, so the same lever on JD has a different, much shorter ceiling.
frontier.next_probe: Port KD's out-of-loop second set of `idx` onto chassis_jd_inline_index_arith.c and sweep its placements (before the outer loop, in the outer loop's init, in the outer loop's update, after the loops) with the s9c/sweep32.py harness, measuring each with the honest sandbox. Watch instruction count: the lever is only interesting at 78.

frontier.hypothesis: The *3 sum can be expanded with a target that is neither operand and still land in `idx`'s pseudo without a staging copy -- the NON-staging member of the family whose staging member is now banned.
frontier.mechanism: optabs.c:403-421 swaps a commutative pair whenever the expansion target IS op1, so `idx = <x> + idx;` can never emit the target's operand order; with target == 0 the order is already correct (JD proves it). The missing piece is a C construct whose assignment does not pass `to_rtx` down as the RHS expansion target -- expr.c's expand_assignment / store_expr have such paths (want_value, RHS containing a CALL, safe_from_p clearing `target`) -- while still leaving reg_n_sets[idx] == 2.
frontier.next_probe: Read expr.c's expand_assignment and store_expr, enumerate the C spellings that reach those paths (e.g. an assignment whose RHS also contains one of the rand() calls, or the sum as the value of a comma expression), and measure each on the SB chassis. Any spelling that is a variable-staging respelling is the BANNED construct and must not be proposed.

frontier.hypothesis: The halfword-offset quantity can be steered off $s0 by an ordinary C-level copy relationship, closing the byte-offset route (DA/KB, 12/78).
frontier.mechanism: The halfword offset needs a callee-save only because it is live across all four rand() calls; once the byte offset is routed into `idx` it is the only block-local call-crossing quantity and find_free_reg takes $s0 by reg_alloc_order. local-alloc.c:2205-2270 tries qty_phys_copy_sugg / qty_phys_sugg FIRST, so a suggestion for $s1 would restore the target's allocation -- which the target itself proves exists (its halfword offset is block-local and sits in $s1).
frontier.next_probe: Dump .lreg with BB2_SUGG_DEBUG / BB2_QTY_DEBUG on the KB build to see which quantities local-alloc ranks and what copy suggestions exist, then re-measure KB/DA with the halfword offset written to participate in a real copy relationship.
